name: Incheon China Town
desc: Three short walks in Incheon's open-port quarter, 2 minutes from Incheon Station (line 1): the China Town main street, the Songwol-dong Fairy Tale Village loop and the Japanese-style street, plus the two mural streets and the Incheon Citizens' House.

line.name: China Town main street: 1st Paeru → Chinatown-ro → 3rd Paeru, 0.3 km

segments.label: Chinatown-ro via the 1st gate, Uiseondang and Gonghwachun (pedestrian router on OSM streets)

pins.name: Start – Incheon Station (인천역)
pins.desc: Line 1 terminus and Suin-Bundang line. The red Chinese gate is straight across the plaza.

pins.name: 1st Paeru gate – Junghwaga (제1패루 중화가)
pins.desc: The main gate of Korea's oldest China Town (1883). Walk uphill along Chinatown-ro between the red lanterns.

pins.name: Jajangmyeon Museum (짜장면박물관)
pins.desc: In the former Gonghwachun restaurant where jajangmyeon was born. Small fee, 20 min.

pins.name: Uiseondang temple (의선당)
pins.desc: A small Chinese temple of 1893, just off the main street on the left.

pins.name: Gonghwachun restaurant (공화춘)
pins.desc: The best-known jajangmyeon house on the street; expect a queue at lunch.

pins.name: End – 3rd Paeru gate, Seollinmun (제3패루 선린문)
pins.desc: Top of the main street. The Chu-Han mural street starts here, and Jayu Park is up the steps to the right.

line.name: Fairy Tale Village loop: entrance → Donghwamaeul-gil → Donghwamaeul-angil → entrance, 0.6 km

segments.label: Loop through the village streets (pedestrian router on OSM streets)

pins.name: Start / End – Fairy Tale Village entrance (동화마을 입구)
pins.desc: Three-way junction at the top of China Town, 5 min from Incheon Station. Walk the loop clockwise.

pins.name: Fairy Tale Village centre (송월동 동화마을)
pins.desc: Houses painted with fairy-tale scenes: Pinocchio, Snow White, the Little Prince. Best photos in the side alleys; free, open all day.

line.name: Japanese-style street: boundary stairs → Sinpo-ro 23beon-gil → Open Port museums, 0.2 km

segments.label: Sinpo-ro 23beon-gil past the museums (pedestrian router on OSM streets)

pins.name: Start – Qing–Japan concession boundary stairs (청일조계지 경계계단)
pins.desc: The 1880s stone stairway that divided the Chinese and Japanese settlements: Chinese lanterns on the left, Japanese wooden façades on the right.

pins.name: Japanese-style street (일본풍거리)
pins.desc: Former Japanese bank and trading-house façades restored along Sinpo-ro 23beon-gil.

pins.name: Incheon Open Port Museum (인천개항박물관)
pins.desc: In the old Japanese 1st Bank (1899). Korea's first customs, railway and post exhibits.

pins.name: End – Modern Architecture Exhibition Hall (개항장 근대건축전시관)
pins.desc: In the old Japanese 18th Bank (1890). Incheon Art Platform and Sinpo Market are a few minutes further on.

pins.name: Chu-Han mural street (초한지 벽화거리)
pins.desc: Murals of the Chu–Han war, from the 3rd Paeru up along Jayugongwon-seo-ro towards Jayu Park.

pins.name: Three Kingdoms mural street (삼국지 벽화거리)
pins.desc: 77 panels telling the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, along the lane between China Town and the boundary stairs.

pins.name: Incheon Citizens' House (인천시민애집)
pins.desc: Former mayor's residence (1966) on the site of a Japanese merchant's villa, now a free cultural space with a garden view over the port. Below Jayu Park, 5 min from the Japanese street.
